note: Distinguishing Stolerman syndrome (KDM6B) from Kabuki syndrome (KDM6A/KMT2D) via hallmark dysmorphic features like fetal pads and eversion is clinically relevant and grounded in literature.

evidence.text: Heterozygous variants in KDM6B cause neurodevelopmental disorder with coarse facies and mild distal skeletal abnormalities (Stolerman neurodevelopmental syndrome).

source.title: The clinical and molecular spectrum of the KDM6B-related neurodevelopmental disorder
source.quote: According to OMIM, heterozygous variants in KDM6B cause “neurodevelopmental disorder with coarse facies and mild distal skeletal abnormalities.”

evidence.text: Kabuki syndrome is caused by variants in histone modification genes including KDM6A and KMT2D, presenting with characteristic facial and developmental phenotypes.

source.title: From Genotype to Phenotype – A Review ...
source.quote: Kabuki syndrome (KS) is a rare neuro-developmental disorder caused by variants in genes of histone modification, including KMT2D and KDM6A.
